title: Add an admin user with sudo and an SSH key
tasks: add ssh key for a user

USER.means: the new account name, e.g. alice

steps.say: The name is free: no output means free.
Create the user; it asks for a password and details.
steps.rollback: Remove the user and their home folder:

steps.say: Allow sudo: add the user to the group sudo.
Create the .ssh folder, owned by the user, private.
Paste the user's PUBLIC key (one line starting ssh-ed25519 or ssh-rsa).
The key file must belong to the user and be private, or SSH ignores it.
The user is in the sudo group.
What the user may run with sudo.

pitfalls: Test a new SSH login in a second terminal before you log out of the first.
The group change applies at the user's next login.
